headlines.text: Flash back to 2023, when the AEW TNT Title found a new home as Christian Cage vs. Darby Allin vs. Luchasaurus battled it out, appearing on Collision, rated 7.44 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. In a chaotic title mix-up, Christian Cage briefly lost the TNT Title to his own partner Luchasaurus mid-match, only for Luchasaurus to hand it back and let Cage steal the pin on him moments later, uniting the belt under Cage as undisputed champion.

Rewind to 2022, when AEW welcomed Jack Perry for the first time against Rey Fenix, appearing on Rampage, rated 7.94 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle. Now billed as "Jungle Boy" Jack Perry instead of just Jungle Boy ? a deliberate rebrand ? he beat Rey Fenix as his feud with Christian Cage and a betraying Luchasaurus deepened.
On a Wednesday in 2020, back when Kip Sabian was back in action after just over 3 months away, appearing on Dynamite.

secondaries.text: On a Saturday in 2023, back when Bryan Danielson vs. Ricky Starks settled things in a Texas Death Match, closing out the card as the main event on Collision, rated 8.54 ? an outstanding performance from both sides. In a brutal Texas Death Match, Danielson busted Starks open with chair shots and finished the war with a running Busaiku Knee.
Rewind to 2022, when AEW welcomed Action Bronson for the first time, appearing on Rampage, rated 5.62.

Turning the clock back to 2022: Ricky Starks vs. Powerhouse Hobbs settled things in a Lights Out match, serving as the night's main event on Rampage, rated 7.38 ? a well-worked match in a hard-fought men's division clash ? part of that year's Grand Slam '22 - Night 2.
